newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries close higher after busy session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries close higher after busy session.

text.p: The prices of U.S. Treasury securities closed higher following a busy trading session on Wednesday.

July retail sales data came in close to expectations with a rise of 0.6 percent, and 0.5 percent increase excluding autos. Producer prices in July fell 0.1 percent -- the seventh consecutive monthly decline and below analysts' forecasts.
Those figures gave the bond market a strong bid in early trading.

Prices fell sharply following an initial surge after release of the early data as short selling and dollar weakness led to large sales by European holders, traders said, before regaining momentum in afternoon trading.
Analysts said much the of sales seen were due to technical factors, which kicked back later in the session to help support the market.
"The economy is picking up. August retail sales are likely to be stronger," said Mickey Levy, chief financial economist at Nationsbanc Capital Markets Inc.
The market likely had built in its worst fears about retail sales and Wednesday's bouceback in prices was a relief reaction, he said.
Levy saw no inflationary threat in the consumer price index, scheduled for release on Thursday.
He also saw a continuation of the recovery that started in April of 1991.
"The market seems to be going back and forth. It usually overdoes things going either way," said Wayne Ayers, chief economist at Bank of Boston, of this session's market movement.

He said the market would continue to look to the pace of economic growth in the third quarter in attempting to find a suitable trading range. He saw third quarter growth at about 3.0 percent, a pickup from the second quarter but still well below the first quarter's torrid rate of growth.
Ayers saw the Federal Reserve moving to tighten monetary policy again during its September FOMC meeting.
"They have not abandoned their preemptive stance and (another tightening) is likely before the end of the year," Ayers said.

Under the leadership of Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, the central bank has never voted to either ease or tighten monetary policy only once, analysts pointed out, making another tightening quite likely.
Trading volume was heavy with GovPX reporting that volume was almost 20 percent above average, though it did slow in the afternoon.
The Treasury's 30-year issue was ending up 16/32 at 96-21/3 to yield 6.63 percent.

At the short end of the maturity spectrum, three-month bills were up 2/32 to yield 5.19 percent. Six-month bills were down three basis points at 5.20 percent and year bills were off four basis points at 5.28 percent.
The 10-year issue was up 12/32 at 98-11/32 to yield 6.36 percent. The five-year was 8/32 higher at 99-7/32 to yield 6.18 percent and the two-year 4/32 higher to yield 5.94 percent.
